originality.rationale: Published regular-graph majority-of-majorities and qualitative bipartite minority-control results are explicitly acknowledged; they do not determine the complete split-graph inversion distribution. General binomial election-inversion papers partition voters into disjoint states, unlike the massively overlapping voting neighborhoods used here. Published matched-source and semantic result searches found no statement implying the exact two-binomial distribution or the zero-to-quarter transition. Residual unindexed-monopoly literature risk remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may appear in older graph-voting and majority-monopoly literature not identified by these searches.
The 2019 elite-monopoly proceedings full text was not available in the checked materials; only the university abstract was read.
The graph family is special; novelty is asserted for the exact finite and Gaussian inversion law, not the general phenomenon of minority control.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp group-size boundary for whether locally consulted voters recover the original electorate majority and computes the actual representation-error probability on the non-faithful side. The 0-to-25% jump when one vertex changes class at fixed odd order is a mathematically motivated network-design effect, not an arbitrary finite calculation. The complete exact count and general ratio limit quantify risk beyond existence of a controlling minority.
